activity_context.topic_title: Reducing a Quadratic Curve to Its Principal Axes

feedback.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation $24{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+21{x}_{2}^{2}=100?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Consider the quadratic form $Q(x)=24{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+21{x}_{2}^{2}.$ To determine the curve defined by the given equation, we reduce $Q(x)$ to its canonical (diagonal) form.  

First, we write down the matrix of $Q(x),$ which is

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}24 & 2 \\ 2 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we find the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}24-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 21-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-45\lambda +500 & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,20\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, our quadratic form can be reduced to $25{y}_{1}^{2}+20{y}_{2}^{2}.$  

In the new variables, the curve has the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}25{y}_{1}^{2}+20{y}_{2}^{2} & =100 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{5} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes   $2$ and $\sqrt{5}.$
